correctness.rationale: For each n>=3, every chosen pair of nonadjacent vertices in K_3 square K_n has exactly two possible internal geodesic vertices. Thus the only obstruction is an all-occupied 2x2 rectangle. Each column of cardinality two consumes one of three row-pair types; a column of cardinality three consumes all. Enumerating the only disjoint permissible cases yields the full visibility polynomial. By monotonicity, maximality is checked by single-vertex additions. Empty and all-singleton columns, or one double column, are extendible; with two distinct double types the singleton row must lie outside the one unused pair; three distinct types or a triple column are fully saturated. The disjoint families yield both maximal coefficients. Under S3 x Sn, singleton multiplicities are unordered triples, giving the partition count. An independent subset/geodesic script exhausts 2,396,672 subset patterns for n=3..7, with separate geodesic checks of 37,376 patterns for n=3..5. The infinite statement is proved structurally, not inferred from finite testing.

originality.rationale: The 2021 full text proves the forbidden-rectangle characterization and reduces maximum cardinality to Zarankiewicz numbers; the 2023 full text establishes the smallest maximal cardinality. The 2024 diameter-two study provides additional scalar extremal reductions. The 2025 visibility-polynomial paper defines the invariant, gives a general inclusion-exclusion method, and computes other families. None of these inspected passages supplies a closed cardinality polynomial for all 3-by-n rook-graph visibility sets, exhaustive maximal-set trichotomy, counts of both strata, or subgroup-orbit enumeration. The new counting result is not a verbal restatement of the known scalar bounds or generic inclusion-exclusion, although it follows from the already known rectangle criterion after a nontrivial enumeration. Targeted mathematical-record and terminology searches found no direct covering statement, but absence is not a proof of global priority.

value.rationale: Full all-cardinality visibility polynomials and inclusion-maximal enumerators for a natural infinite Cartesian-product family extend the established extremal-size-only analyses. Width three is the first case with three competing row-pair resources, and the classified saturation types yield genuinely distinct n+2 and n+3 maximal strata and their exact symmetry-orbit counts. These data identify every optimal/minimal maximal pattern and provide concrete enumerators for further graph-polynomial and bipartite C4-saturation work, beyond recomputing the known scalar bounds.
